```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

```{r model-meta, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
ui <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Amice_2021_nicotine_pbpk"))
cat("* Citation: ", ui$reference, "\n", sep = "")
cat("* Description: ", ui$description, "\n", sep = "")
```

* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2021.688597> (open access, PMC8329445)
* Supplementary material (DataSheet 1: equations; DataSheet 2: Tables S.1-S.3):
  <https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fphar.2021.688597/full#supplementary-material>

Amice 2021 is a short research report on a whole-body PBPK model for nicotine
and its main metabolite cotinine, written in MATLAB and solved with `ode45`. The
paper presents two models: a baseline adult model for a non-pregnant woman, and
a pregnancy (p-PBPK) model that adds mammary, uterus, placenta and a fetus. Only
the **baseline non-pregnant model** is packaged here. The pregnancy model cannot
be reproduced from the published material; the reasons are listed under
[Assumptions and deviations](#assumptions-and-deviations).

# Population

The model is a physiological simulation, not a fit to individual data. The
baseline woman weighs 70 kg (Results, "Baseline PBPK Model", following the
adult configuration of Robinson 1992). Her hepatic and renal clearances are the
Dempsey 2002 values for women (Table 1, column 2). Her organ volumes and blood
flows are the adult fractions of Supplementary Table S.1, and her drug-specific
partition coefficients, unbound fractions and blood:plasma ratios come from
Supplementary Table S.3.

The authors checked the baseline model against two published intravenous
studies in non-smokers: plasma nicotine and cotinine in six subjects given
nicotine at 10 ug/min for 60 min (Curvall 1990), and plasma cotinine in four
subjects given cotinine at 0.67 mg/min for 30 min (De Schepper 1987).

The same information is available programmatically:

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Amice_2021_nicotine_pbpk")()$population)
```

# Source trace

Each `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source. The table
collects them. "DS1" is Supplementary DataSheet 1 (the equations) and "DS2" is
Supplementary DataSheet 2 (Tables S.1-S.3).

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| Arterial blood, `d/dt(a_arterial)` | n/a | DS1 Eq 1 (nicotine), Eq 12 (cotinine) |
| Fat, slowly perfused, rapidly perfused, brain | n/a | DS1 Eqs 2-5 and 13-16 |
| Kidney, with renal clearance `fu * CL_renal * C_K / K_K` | n/a | DS1 Eqs 8 and 19 |
| Liver, with hepatic clearance `fu * CL_hep * C_Li / K_Li` | n/a | DS1 Eqs 9 and 20 |
| Cotinine formation `0.8 * fuN * CLN_Li * CN_Li / KN_Li` | n/a | DS1 Eq 20 |
| Lung | n/a | DS1 Eqs 10 and 21 |
| Venous blood, with the intravenous dose input | n/a | DS1 Eqs 11 and 22 |
| `qcc` (cardiac output = `qcc * WT^0.75`) | 15.126 L/h/kg^0.75 | DS2 Table S.1, FCO |
| `fvol_arterial`, `fvol_venous` | 0.02, 0.0571 | DS2 Table S.1 |
| `fvol_fat`, `fvol_slowly_perfused`, `fvol_rapidly_perfused` | 0.187, 0.536, 0.032 | DS2 Table S.1 |
| `fvol_brain`, `fvol_kidney`, `fvol_liver`, `fvol_lung` | 0.021, 0.004, 0.026, 0.008 | DS2 Table S.1 |
| `fq_fat`, `fq_slowly_perfused`, `fq_rapidly_perfused` | 0.052, 0.188, 0.216 | DS2 Table S.1 |
| `fq_brain`, `fq_kidney`, `fq_liver` | 0.117, 0.177, 0.25 | DS2 Table S.1 |
| `lclint`, `lcl_renal` (nicotine) | log(16.2), log(0.7) mL/min/kg | Table 1, women; DS2 Table S.3 |
| `lclint_cot`, `lcl_renal_cot` (cotinine) | log(0.5), log(0.2) mL/min/kg | Table 1, women; DS2 Table S.3 |
| `fu`, `fu_cot` | 0.95, 0.974 | DS2 Table S.3 |
| `bpr`, `bpr_cot` | 0.8, 0.88 | DS2 Table S.3 |
| `fm` | 0.8 | DS1 Eq 20; Methods ("approximately 80%") |
| `lkp_fat`, `lkp_slowly_perfused`, `lkp_rapidly_perfused`, `lkp_brain` | log(1), log(2.5), log(3), log(3) | DS2 Table S.3, nicotine |
| `lkp_kidney`, `lkp_liver`, `lkp_lung` | log(15), log(9), log(2) | DS2 Table S.3, nicotine |
| `lkp_fat_cot`, `lkp_slowly_perfused_cot`, `lkp_rapidly_perfused_cot`, `lkp_brain_cot` | log(0.5), log(0.85), log(1.5), log(1.5) | DS2 Table S.3, cotinine |
| `lkp_kidney_cot`, `lkp_liver_cot`, `lkp_lung_cot` | log(2), log(2), log(1) | DS2 Table S.3, cotinine |

# Simulation scenarios

The model is deterministic, so each scenario is a single 70 kg woman. The three
regimens are the ones the paper simulates for the non-pregnant woman.

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Amice_2021_nicotine_pbpk")

# Doses go to the venous blood state of the analyte given. Observation rows
# sit on the same ODE state; rxode2 returns every algebraic output (Cc,
# Cc_cot, Cbrain, ...) at those rows.
make_events <- function(amt, rate, cmt, obs_times, id) {
  dose <- data.frame(id = id, time = 0, evid = 1, amt = amt, rate = rate, cmt = cmt)
  obs <- data.frame(id = id, time = obs_times, evid = 0, amt = 0, rate = 0, cmt = cmt)
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(WT = 70)
}

# Scenario 1 (Figure 2A): nicotine 10 ug/min for 60 min = 600 ug at 600 ug/h.
ev_nic <- make_events(600, 600, "a_venous", seq(0, 48, by = 1 / 12), id = 1L)
# Scenario 2 (Figure 2B): cotinine 0.67 mg/min for 30 min = 20100 ug at 40200 ug/h.
ev_cot <- make_events(20100, 40200, "a_venous_cot", seq(0, 24, by = 1 / 12), id = 2L)
# Scenario 3 (Figure 3A): single intravenous nicotine injection of 1 ug/kg.
ev_bolus <- make_events(70, 0, "a_venous", seq(0, 1, by = 1 / 120), id = 3L)

sim_nic <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_nic))
sim_cot <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_cot))
sim_bolus <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_bolus))
```

## Mass balance

Every nicotine state plus the metabolised-nicotine accumulator must add up to
the dose. Every cotinine state plus the metabolised-cotinine accumulator must
add up to `fm` times the metabolised nicotine. Both sides use the same solve,
so the difference is pure integration error and the bound is tight.

```{r mass-balance}
nic_states <- c(
  "a_arterial", "a_fat", "a_slowly_perfused", "a_rapidly_perfused", "a_brain",
  "a_kidney", "a_liver", "a_lung", "a_venous", "a_urine", "a_hepatic"
)
cot_states <- paste0(setdiff(nic_states, "a_hepatic"), "_cot")
mb <- sim_nic |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= 1) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    nic_total = rowSums(dplyr::pick(dplyr::all_of(nic_states))),
    cot_total = rowSums(dplyr::pick(dplyr::all_of(c(cot_states, "a_hepatic_cot"))))
  )
stopifnot(
  max(abs(mb$nic_total - 600)) < 1e-3,
  max(abs(mb$cot_total - 0.8 * mb$a_hepatic)) < 1e-3
)
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 2A: nicotine infusion, plasma nicotine and cotinine

The maintainers digitised the authors' model curves (blue and red lines) from
Figure 2A. The model output overlaid below is plasma (blood divided by the
Table S.3 blood:plasma ratio).

```{r fig2a}
fig2a <- tibble::tribble(
  ~time_min, ~analyte,   ~paper,
  15,        "Nicotine", 2.07,
  30,        "Nicotine", 3.40,
  45,        "Nicotine", 4.26,
  100,       "Nicotine", 2.55,
  150,       "Nicotine", 1.94,
  200,       "Nicotine", 1.60,
  250,       "Nicotine", 1.32,
  295,       "Nicotine", 1.12,
  45,        "Cotinine", 2.18,
  100,       "Cotinine", 3.95,
  200,       "Cotinine", 4.96
)

sim_fig2a <- sim_nic |>
  dplyr::filter(time <= 5) |>
  dplyr::select(time, Nicotine = Cc, Cotinine = Cc_cot) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc")

ggplot(sim_fig2a, aes(time * 60, conc, colour = analyte)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = fig2a, aes(time_min, paper), shape = 4, size = 2.5) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(0.1, 10)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (min)", y = "Plasma concentration (ug/L)", colour = NULL,
    title = "Nicotine 10 ug/min for 60 min, 70 kg woman",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2A of Amice 2021. Crosses: authors' model curves, digitised."
  )
```

```{r fig2a-table}
fig2a_cmp <- fig2a |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    model = mapply(
      function(t, a) {
        col <- if (a == "Nicotine") "Cc" else "Cc_cot"
        stats::approx(sim_nic$time * 60, sim_nic[[col]], xout = t)$y
      },
      time_min, analyte
    ),
    pct_diff = 100 * (model / paper - 1)
  )

fig2a_cmp |>
  dplyr::mutate(model = round(model, 2), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Time (min)" = time_min, "Analyte" = analyte,
    "Figure 2A (ug/L)" = paper, "Model (ug/L)" = model, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Model plasma concentrations against the digitised Figure 2A curves.")

# After the infusion (100 min onwards) and for cotinine throughout, the model
# reproduces the authors' curves within digitisation error (observed range
# -0.2% to +5.5%). During the nicotine infusion it does not: see the deviations.
post <- dplyr::filter(fig2a_cmp, analyte == "Cotinine" | time_min >= 100)
stopifnot(max(abs(post$pct_diff)) < 12)
```

## Urinary recovery at 5 h

The paper states its model's urinary recovery 5 h after the start of the
nicotine infusion: 28.8 ug unchanged nicotine and 15.3 ug cotinine (Results,
"Baseline PBPK Model"). Curvall 1990 measured 22 +/- 7.2 ug and 16.1 +/- 3.8 ug.

```{r urine}
at5 <- dplyr::filter(sim_nic, abs(time - 5) < 1e-8)
urine <- tibble::tibble(
  Analyte = c("Nicotine", "Cotinine"),
  `Amice 2021 model (ug)` = c(28.8, 15.3),
  `Curvall 1990 observed (ug)` = c("22 +/- 7.2", "16.1 +/- 3.8"),
  `This model (ug)` = round(c(at5$a_urine, at5$a_urine_cot), 1)
)
knitr::kable(urine, caption = "Cumulative urinary excretion 0-5 h after nicotine 10 ug/min for 60 min.")

stopifnot(
  abs(at5$a_urine / 28.8 - 1) < 0.03,
  abs(at5$a_urine_cot / 15.3 - 1) < 0.08
)
```

## Figure 2B: cotinine infusion

Figure 2B shows the authors' model (blue) and De Schepper 1987's observed
plasma cotinine (red), both digitised by the maintainers.

```{r fig2b}
fig2b <- tibble::tribble(
  ~time, ~paper_model, ~observed,
  1,     292,          383,
  2,     260,          328,
  5,     226,          276,
  10,    175,          220,
  20,    106,          129,
  23.5,  89,           107
)

fig2b_cmp <- fig2b |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    plasma = stats::approx(sim_cot$time, sim_cot$Cc_cot, xout = time)$y,
    blood = stats::approx(sim_cot$time, sim_cot$Cblood_cot, xout = time)$y
  )

sim_cot |>
  dplyr::select(time, `Model, plasma` = Cc_cot, `Model, whole blood` = Cblood_cot) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "series", values_to = "conc") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, conc)) +
  geom_line(aes(linetype = series)) +
  geom_point(data = fig2b, aes(time, paper_model, colour = "Amice 2021 model"), shape = 4, size = 2.5) +
  geom_point(data = fig2b, aes(time, observed, colour = "De Schepper 1987 observed"), size = 2) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(10, 1000)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Cotinine (ug/L)", colour = "Digitised", linetype = NULL,
    title = "Cotinine 0.67 mg/min for 30 min, 70 kg woman",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2B of Amice 2021."
  )

fig2b_cmp |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(plasma, blood), \(x) round(x, 0))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Time (h)" = time, "Figure 2B model (ug/L)" = paper_model,
    "De Schepper observed (ug/L)" = observed,
    "This model, plasma (ug/L)" = plasma, "This model, blood (ug/L)" = blood
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Cotinine after the cotinine infusion.")

# The level is offset (see the deviations); the terminal slope is not. Both
# the digitised curve and the model give a 10-20 h half-life of about 13-14 h.
hl <- function(t, c) log(2) * diff(t) / -diff(log(c))
hl_paper <- hl(fig2b$time[c(4, 5)], fig2b$paper_model[c(4, 5)])
hl_model <- hl(fig2b_cmp$time[c(4, 5)], fig2b_cmp$plasma[c(4, 5)])
c(paper = hl_paper, model = hl_model)
stopifnot(abs(hl_model / hl_paper - 1) < 0.15)
```

## Figure 3A: maternal brain after a 1 ug/kg nicotine injection

Figure 3A shows maternal brain concentrations after a single 1 ug/kg
intravenous nicotine injection, for the pregnant and the non-pregnant woman.
The maintainers digitised all four curves. By the legend, the solid line is
pregnant nicotine, the dotted line non-pregnant nicotine, the dashed line
pregnant cotinine and the blue line non-pregnant cotinine.

```{r fig3a}
fig3a <- tibble::tribble(
  ~time_min, ~analyte,   ~solid_or_dashed, ~dotted_or_blue,
  2.5,       "Nicotine", 4.65,             6.46,
  5,         "Nicotine", 4.32,             6.11,
  10,        "Nicotine", 3.54,             5.09,
  20,        "Nicotine", 2.24,             3.35,
  30,        "Nicotine", 1.53,             2.28,
  45,        "Nicotine", 1.04,             1.53,
  10,        "Cotinine", 0.318,            0.268,
  20,        "Cotinine", 0.484,            0.432,
  30,        "Cotinine", 0.521,            0.471,
  45,        "Cotinine", 0.531,            0.498
)

fig3a_cmp <- fig3a |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    model = mapply(
      function(t, a) {
        col <- if (a == "Nicotine") "Cbrain" else "Cbrain_cot"
        stats::approx(sim_bolus$time * 60, sim_bolus[[col]], xout = t)$y
      },
      time_min, analyte
    ),
    pct_vs_solid_or_dashed = 100 * (model / solid_or_dashed - 1),
    pct_vs_dotted_or_blue = 100 * (model / dotted_or_blue - 1)
  )

sim_bolus |>
  dplyr::select(time, Nicotine = Cbrain, Cotinine = Cbrain_cot) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  dplyr::filter(conc > 1e-3) |>
  ggplot(aes(time * 60, conc, colour = analyte)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = fig3a, aes(time_min, solid_or_dashed, shape = "Solid / dashed (legend: pregnant)"), size = 2.5) +
  geom_point(data = fig3a, aes(time_min, dotted_or_blue, shape = "Dotted / blue (legend: non-pregnant)"), size = 2.5) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(4, 1)) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(1e-3, 10)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (min)", y = "Brain concentration (ug/L)", colour = NULL, shape = "Figure 3A curve",
    title = "Single intravenous nicotine injection, 1 ug/kg, 70 kg woman",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3A of Amice 2021. Points: digitised curves."
  )

fig3a_cmp |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    model = signif(model, 3),
    dplyr::across(dplyr::starts_with("pct_"), \(x) round(x, 1))
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Time (min)" = time_min, "Analyte" = analyte,
    "Solid / dashed (ug/L)" = solid_or_dashed, "Dotted / blue (ug/L)" = dotted_or_blue,
    "Model (ug/L)" = model,
    "Model vs solid / dashed (%)" = pct_vs_solid_or_dashed,
    "Model vs dotted / blue (%)" = pct_vs_dotted_or_blue
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Model brain concentrations against the digitised Figure 3A curves.")

tmax_brain_min <- 60 * sim_bolus$time[which.max(sim_bolus$Cbrain)]
c(peak_brain_nicotine = max(sim_bolus$Cbrain), tmax_min = tmax_brain_min)

# Model brain nicotine reproduces the SOLID curve at every digitised point
# (observed -2.4% to +5.0%); see the deviations for why the legend calls it
# the pregnant curve. The digitised peak of both curves is at 2.5-3 min; the
# text says 'within 2 min'.
nic3a <- dplyr::filter(fig3a_cmp, analyte == "Nicotine")
stopifnot(
  max(abs(nic3a$pct_vs_solid_or_dashed)) < 10,
  tmax_brain_min <= 3
)
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports a nicotine peak at about 1 h, a nicotine half-life of about
3 h and a cotinine half-life of about 16 h (Results, "Baseline PBPK Model"). The
nicotine values come from the 5-h window of Figure 2A; the cotinine half-life
is taken from the 24-h cotinine infusion of Figure 2B.

```{r pknca}
nca_input <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_nic |>
    dplyr::filter(time <= 5) |>
    dplyr::transmute(id = 1L, time, Cc, treatment = "Nicotine, nicotine infusion"),
  sim_cot |>
    dplyr::transmute(id = 2L, time, Cc = Cc_cot, treatment = "Cotinine, cotinine infusion")
) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc))

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_input, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_df <- tibble::tibble(
  id = c(1L, 2L), time = 0, amt = c(600, 20100),
  treatment = c("Nicotine, nicotine infusion", "Cotinine, cotinine infusion")
)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)

intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
```

## Comparison against the published values

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,                     ~tmax, ~half.life,
  "Nicotine, nicotine infusion",  1,     3,
  "Cotinine, cotinine infusion",  NA,    16
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  params = c("tmax", "half.life"),
  units = c(tmax = "h", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated against published values. * differs from reference by >20%.")

res <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result)
get_par <- function(trt, par) res$PPORRES[res$treatment == trt & res$PPTESTCD == par]
stopifnot(
  abs(get_par("Nicotine, nicotine infusion", "tmax") - 1) < 0.1,
  abs(get_par("Nicotine, nicotine infusion", "half.life") / 3 - 1) < 0.2,
  abs(get_par("Cotinine, cotinine infusion", "half.life") / 16 - 1) < 0.2
)
```

The nicotine peak time and half-life agree with the paper. The cotinine
half-life is shorter than the rounded "~16 h" of the text but matches the
terminal slope of the authors' own Figure 2B curve (previous section), which is
about 13-14 h.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Only the non-pregnant baseline model is packaged.** The pregnancy model
  could not be reproduced from the published material, for five reasons:
  1. The main text and Table S.2 describe placental transfer as an
     influx-efflux model with four transfer constants Kt1-Kt4 (1500, 1000, 880
     and 1000 L/h), but none of Kt1-Kt4 appears in the 32 printed equations.
     The placental and fetal-blood equations (DS1 Eqs 23, 24, 28 and 32)
     instead use a Michaelis-Menten exchange term scaled by a coefficient PAF.
  2. PAF, the placental partition coefficients and the fetal cardiac output
     (printed as "FQblood-fetus = L/h/kg", with no number) are not given
     anywhere. The fetal blood fraction is 0.0085 on the equations page and
     0.085 in Table S.2.
  3. The printed equations have defects: Eq 24 (placental cotinine) uses the
     arterial nicotine concentration, the venous equations have no placental
     return, and the "fetal clearance 20% of maternal" assumption of the
     Results has no term in fetal Eqs 25-32.
  4. The "muscle clearance" update mentioned in the Methods has no value.
  5. Swapping in only the pregnant clearances of Table 1 (column 3) at 73 kg
     lowers plasma nicotine and cotinine at 150 min by about 22% and 1%. The
     paper reports about 70% and 30%, so a mother-only pregnant variant would
     not reproduce the paper and is not offered.
  The pregnancy model will be added if the authors' MATLAB code becomes
  available.
- **Mammary and uterus compartments are omitted.** They appear in DS1 Eqs 6-7
  and 17-18 but are pregnancy compartments (Table S.2); the adult Table S.1
  lists no volume or flow for them, and the adult flow fractions already sum
  to 1.
- **The infusion compartment `Vit` is not implemented.** Table S.1 lists a
  `Vit` volume (0.0214 of body weight) and Table S.3 a transfer rate Kvit of
  4.1 /min, but no equation uses them: Eq 11 doses the venous blood directly.
  The model follows the equations.
- **Plasma versus blood.** The equations track blood. `Cc` and `Cc_cot` are
  blood divided by the Table S.3 blood:plasma ratios (0.8 and 0.88), the
  reading that matches the post-infusion curves of Figure 2A. Whole-blood
  outputs `Cblood` and `Cblood_cot` are also returned.
- **Nicotine during the infusion.** Up to the end of the nicotine infusion, the
  authors' Figure 2A curve rises more slowly than this model: about 2.1 vs 4.3
  ug/L at 15 min, and a peak of about 5.5 vs 7.5 ug/L at 60 min. From 100 min
  on the two agree within digitisation error, and the paper's printed urinary
  recoveries are reproduced. The published equations do not explain the early
  difference. Reading Kvit as 4.1 /h instead of 4.1 /min reproduces the first
  15 min but overshoots every later point, so the maintainers did not adopt it.
- **Cotinine level after the cotinine infusion.** The authors' Figure 2B model
  curve is about 20% below this model's whole-blood cotinine and about 30%
  below its plasma cotinine at every time after 1 h, with the same terminal
  slope. This model's whole-blood cotinine lies close to De Schepper's
  observed data. The published material does not explain the offset. The
  figure title gives the infusion rate as 0.65 mg/min and the text as 0.67
  mg/min; the text value is used, and the 3% difference does not account for
  the offset.
- **Figure 3A brain nicotine.** This non-pregnant model reproduces the solid
  nicotine curve of Figure 3A within about 5% at every digitised point. The
  figure legend assigns that curve to the pregnant woman and the dotted curve,
  about 1.4 times higher, to the non-pregnant woman. The maintainers could not
  determine whether the line styles in the legend are swapped. The two curves
  also differ much less than the pregnant and non-pregnant plasma curves of
  Figure 2A (about 0.7 vs 0.3 at comparable times), so Figure 3A cannot settle
  the question. The model brain cotinine lies within about 20% of both
  cotinine curves.
- **Clearance units and the "men" column.** The clearances are the women's
  values of Table 1 (mL/min/kg), multiplied by body weight. The "men" column
  (Curvall 1990 / Robinson 1992) is printed in mL/h/kg in Table 1 but in
  kg^0.25/h and L/h/kg^0.75 in Table S.1. It is not used, because the
  paper's baseline is a woman. The Figure 2A caption says "adult men", but its
  title says "adult female plasma", and the women's clearances reproduce the
  paper's urinary recoveries.
- **Cotinine formation on a mass basis.** Eq 20 forms cotinine at 0.8 times the
  hepatic nicotine elimination rate in mass units, with no correction for the
  molecular weights (162.2 and 176.2 g/mol). The model follows the equation.
- **No variability.** The paper reports no between-subject variability and no
  residual error, so none is declared.
- **Digitised values.** The Figure 2A, 2B and 3A values above were digitised by
  the maintainers from the published figures. They carry a reading
  uncertainty of a few percent.
- No correction notice for the article was found on the journal page or in
  PubMed as of 2026-10-16.
